{{short description|Argentine chemist}}

'''Silvia Elsa Braslavsky''' (born April 5, 1942 in [[Buenos Aires]]) is an [[Argentina|Argentine]] chemist.<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = http://www.mpibac.mpg.de/bac/mitarbeiter/Alumni/braslavsky/braslavsky_en.php
 |title       = Max Planck Society CV
 |accessdate  = 16 December 2012
 |url-status     = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20110511193238/http://www.mpibac.mpg.de/bac/mitarbeiter/Alumni/braslavsky/braslavsky_en.php
 |archivedate = 11 May 2011
}}</ref>
She is the daughter of educationist {{Ill|Berta Perelstein de Braslavsky|es|Berta Perelstein de Braslavsky}} and biochemist Lázaro Braslavsky, and the sister of [[Cecilia Braslavsky]], educationist and erstwhile director of the [[International Bureau of Education]] of UNESCO. She has two daughters, sociologist [[Paula-Irene Villa Braslavsky]] and Carolina Klockow.

Braslavsky has worked extensively in the domain of [[photobiology]] and she is a specialist in experimental photooptoacoustics. She was senior research scientist and Professor at the [[Max Planck Institute for Bioinorganic Chemistry|Max Planck Institute for Radiation Chemistry]] (now renamed ''Bioinorganic Chemistry'') until her retirement in 2007.

== Scientific career ==

Braslavsky read chemistry at the [[University of Buenos Aires]] but left Argentina after the [[La Noche de los Bastones Largos|"night of the long batons"]]. While being a research assistant in [[Santiago de Chile]] she defended her PhD at the University of Buenos Aires. Following temporary positions at [[Penn State University]] (1969-1972), the [[National University of Rio Cuarto]], Argentina (1972-1975), again Penn State (1975) and the [[University of Alberta]] in Edmonton, Canada (1975), she moved to the Max Planck Institute for Radiation Chemistry in Mülheim, Germany (1976), where she stayed until her retirement in 2007.

== Functions ==
Braslavsky holds numerous official positions in the scientific field of chemistry. Since 2000 she is the chair of the [[IUPAC]] subcommittee on [[photochemistry]]. Since 2006 she is a corresponding member of [[CONICET]] and is a member of the international scientific advisory committee of INQUIMAE (Institute for Chemistry of Materials, Environment and Energy). Currently, she is chair and main organiser of the 16th International Conference on Photobiology, to be held in Cordoba, Argentina in 2014.<ref>{{cite web
 |title       = Website of Conference
 |url         = http://www.photobiology2014.com.ar
 |accessdate  = 29 December 2012
 |url-status     = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20130722225822/http://www.photobiology2014.com.ar/
 |archivedate = 22 July 2013
}}</ref>
Since 2010 she is a member of the representative panel of the RCAA (''Red de Científicos Argentinos en Alemania'', i.e. the Network of Argentine Scientists in Germany).

This is selection of her honours and awards:
* 1998 first women to be awarded the Research Award of the [[American Society for Photobiology]].<ref>{{cite web
|title=ASP list of previous award winners
| url=http://www.photobiology.org/UserFiles/File/Awards/ASP%20Research%20Award.pdf
|accessdate=29 December 2012
}}</ref> 
* 2004 Elhuyar-Goldschmidt Prize of the [[:es:Real Sociedad Española de Química|Spanish]] and [[German Chemical Society|German]] chemical society.<ref>{{cite web
 |title       = Press notice of the Max Planck Society
 |url         = http://www.mpibac.mpg.de/bac/neuigkeiten/2004/07/29/forscherpreis_en.php
 |accessdate  = 17 December 2012
 |url-status     = dead

}}</ref> 
* 2008 first woman to be awarded a Doctor Honoris Causa from the [[Universitat Ramon Llull]], Barcelona, Spain.<ref>{{cite web

}}{{dead link|date=March 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

* 2016 Dr. honoris causa Universidad de Buenos Aires, Argentina.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://exactas.uba.ar/silvia-braslavsky-honoris-causa/ |title= Silvia Braslavsky, honoris causa|website=exactas.uba.ar |date= 2 September 2016|access-date=6 June 2022}}{{title missing|date=July 2022}}</ref>

Senior Prize (Moscow).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cadipt.mie.utoronto.ca/ippa/complete-list-of-prize-winners/ |title= Complete List of Prize Winners &#124; Center for Advanced Diffusion-Wave and Photoacoustic Technologies - CADIPTCenter for Advanced Diffusion-Wave and Photoacoustic Technologies – CADIPT|website=cadipt.mie.utoronto.ca |access-date=6 June 2022}}{{title missing|date=July 2022}}</ref>

The EPA established the Award in 2018 to recognize outstanding service to the Photochemistry/Photophysical community. This prize is delivered every two years.

* '"Glossary of Terms Used in Photochemistry'", 3rd Version (IUPAC Recommendations 2006), S.E.Braslavsky, ''Pure Appl. Chem.'' 79, 293-461 (2007). [[doi:10.1351/pac200779030293]]
